הפסקה הזו מציגה את השינוי המבני הגדול של עולם נתוני-האב ב-S/4HANA — ואת ההשלכה המפתיעה שלו: רשומת-הספק (vendor master) שהייתה אובייקט-הליבה של הרכש ב-ERP נבלעת לתוך ה-business partner — מודל אחוד שבו ישות אחת נושאת תפקידים (roles) מרובים: ספק, לקוח, עובד — וזה הכיוון היחיד קדימה. שלוש נקודות מעשיות: ראשית, המודל ניתן ל-back-port לסביבות ERP מעל SAP ERP 6.0 EHP 6 — כלומר אפשר (ולעיתים חובה) לאמץ אותו עוד לפני המעבר ל-S/4HANA; שנית, ההשלכה המפתיעה — ‏SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance, שמנהל זיהוי, ‏onboarding ותחזוקת ספקים, דורש את מודל ה-business partner גם בסביבת ERP: ארגון שרוצה לשלב את פתרון-הענן הזה חייב להריץ את המרת ה-supplier master למודל החדש גם בלי שום כוונת-שדרוג קרובה — עובדה שהופכת את ההמרה מפרויקט-עתיד לדרישת-הווה בחלק מהמפות; ושלישית, ההמרה עצמה ‏(CVI — customer/vendor integration) היא תת-פרויקט אמיתי עם צעדים, בדיקות וסיכונים — שהסעיפים הבאים מפרטים. המסר ליועץ: לשאול על תוכניות-Ariba כבר בשיחת נתוני-האב הראשונה — התשובה משנה את סדר-העבודות.

**הערת יועץ:** ה-business partner בולע את ה-vendor master — הכיוון היחיד קדימה, עם back-port ל-ERP מעל EHP 6; ⚠️ ‏Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance דורש את המודל גם ב-ERP — כלומר תוכניות-Ariba מקדימות את ההמרה גם בלי שדרוג. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, שאלת 'מה תוכניות-Ariba שלכם' שייכת לשיחת נתוני-האב הראשונה — התשובה משנה את סדר-העבודות כולו. יועץ ממצב את ה-CVI כתת-פרויקט עם תקציב ולוח-זמנים משלו, לא כסעיף-אגב.

sections.title: Suppliers as Business Partners
sections.en: 4.3.1 Suppliers as Business Partners Business partners in an SAP ERP environment, as well as in SAP S/4HANA, are entities that transact with the ERP system and your organization. Loosely defined, business partners can be suppliers who sell something to your organization, employees, and/or © 119 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model customers. Sometimes, an individual can represent all three categories. For example, some state and local government entities employ individuals who are maintained in SAP Core Human Capital Management for SAP S/4HANA. These individuals may sell services to the government, such as foster care services, making them a supplier in the system capable of submitting invoices or having checks cut for services rendered. Finally, these individuals could be set up as a customer in the system when requesting assessment or other state government–provided services requiring a fee. Business Partner Objectives The SAP S/4HANA business partner model has the following strategic objectives:  Share general data across different roles.  Support different business partner categories, such as organization, person, or group.  Allow for role versatility; one business partner can perform multiple roles, such as customer and vendor (supplier).  Support multiple addresses for one business partner.  Support time dependency on different subentities, such as roles, addresses, relation- ships, bank data, and so on.  Support relationship flexibility, such as a supplier having a contact person.  Provide a harmonized architecture. There were reasons for creating separate records for each of these relationships in pre- vious versions, a principal one being that sidecar systems such as SAP SRM or SAP Cus- tomer Relationship Management (SAP CRM) only needed a certain type of relationship record to support their dependent transactions—a supplier record or a customer record, respectively. The SAP S/4HANA business partner approach leverages customer/ vendor integration (CVI) to do this translation and delineation for dependent systems while synchronizing changes with the business partner in SAP S/4HANA. The next sec- tion details the creation workflow for a business partner. Business Partner Creation Workflow Per Figure 4.14, a business partner is created whenever a customer or supplier is created in SAP S/4HANA. CVI contains the business partner–specific data, as well as customer and supplier data. Upon commit, the customer and/or vendor data is routed through CVI and combined with business partner data, and the CVI link tables are maintained. Some of the vendor and customer data overlaps; for example, the name and address are contained in both the customer and the vendor record and can be the same for a business partner. 4 Master Data 120 Figure 4.14 Integrated Object Model: Business Partner Customer/Vendor Integration Business Partners in SAP S/4HANA Changing the business partner design impacts the upgrade path from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA. If you’re looking to move suppliers and/or customers to SAP S/4HANA from a previous SAP ERP instance, you must have CVI in place to move to SAP S/4HANA. All cus- tomers, suppliers, and their contacts need to be converted to business partners. Also, whereas before in SAP ERP a user might access a supplier using Transaction XK03, this transaction—along with the others listed in Table 4.3—no longer exists in SAP S/4HANA. Transaction Codes  FD01  FD02  FD03  FD05  FD06  FK01  FK02  FK03  FK05  FK06  MAP1  MAP2  MAP3  MK01  MK02  MK03  MK05  MK06  MK12  MK18  MK19  V-03  V-04  V-05  V-06  V-07  V-08  V-09  V-11  V+21  V+22  V+23  VAP1  VAP2  VAP3  VD01  VD02  VD03  VD05  VD06  XD01  XD02  XD03  XD05  XD06  XD07  XK01  XK02  XK03  XK05  XK06  XK07 Table 4.3 Supplier and Customer Transaction Codes No Longer Used in SAP S/4HANA CVI Complex Interface Business Partner Customer Customer Business Partner CVI Link Tables Customer APIs Vendor APIs Business Partner APIs Customer/Vendor Data Buffer Vendor Vendor (Supplier) Central data Company code data Sales area data SAVE CVI Outbound Get © 121 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model In the best case, if you input a transaction code listed in the following table, you will be redirected to Transaction BP, which is the main transaction for all business partner– related transactions, including supplier and customer records. Transaction BP is thus the single point of entry to create, edit, and display master data for business partners, customers, and vendors in SAP S/4HANA. The business partner number also replaces the supplier and customer numbers. This has further implica- tions for an upgrade and/or data conversion. However, this doesn’t mean that you should collapse all of the existing customer/vendor transactions in SAP ERP into Trans- action BP; there is functionality in SAP ERP transactions not available in Transaction BP, and the SAP ERP help documents refer users to a variety of transactions, which could confuse users if you were to centralize business partner functions in a single transaction in older versions of SAP ERP. In SAP S/4HANA, all of the previous SAP ERP transactions, reports, condition records, and forms that use the customer or vendor number as input fields require the cus- tomer or vendor number, not the business partner number. Even if a new business partner number has been assigned to the customer or vendor, the former customer or vendor number is required. The next section reviews loading supplier records.
sections.he:
‏business partners ב-ERP וב-S/4HANA הם ישויות הסוחרות עם המערכת — ספקים, עובדים, ו/או לקוחות. לעיתים אדם מייצג את כל השלושה. למשל, ישויות ממשל מקומי מעסיקות אנשים ב-SAP Core HCM, שעשויים למכור שירותים (foster care) — ספקים המגישים invoices — וגם להירשם כלקוחות בבקשת שירותים בתשלום.
**Business Partner Objectives:**
• שיתוף נתונים כלליים בין roles.
• תמיכה בקטגוריות (organization, ‏person, ‏group).
• role versatility — ‏business partner אחד במספר roles (customer ו-vendor).
• תמיכה במספר כתובות.
• תלות-זמן בתת-ישויות (roles, כתובות, קשרים, נתוני בנק).
• גמישות קשרים (ספק עם איש קשר).
• ארכיטקטורה מתואמת.
בעבר היו רשומות נפרדות (sidecar systems כמו SAP SRM או SAP CRM נזקקו לסוג קשר מסוים — ספק או לקוח). ה-business partner ממנף customer/vendor integration (CVI) לתרגום למערכות תלויות תוך סנכרון.
**Business Partner Creation Workflow:**
‏business partner נוצר בכל יצירת customer/supplier (Figure 4.14). ‏CVI מכיל נתוני business partner, ‏customer, ו-supplier. ב-commit, נתוני customer/vendor מנותבים דרך CVI ומשולבים, וטבלאות הקישור מתוחזקות. חלק חופף (שם וכתובת בשניהם).
**Business Partners ב-S/4HANA:**
שינוי העיצוב משפיע על נתיב השדרוג. להעברת ספקים/לקוחות ל-S/4HANA, נדרש CVI. כל הספקים, הלקוחות, ואנשי הקשר מומרים ל-business partners. בעוד בעבר ניגשו לספק דרך Transaction XK03, טרנזקציה זו (ועוד ב-טבלה 4.3) אינה קיימת ב-S/4HANA.

**טבלה 4.3 — קודי טרנזקציה (ספק/לקוח) שאינם בשימוש ב-S/4HANA:**
| | |
|---|---|
| FD01-FD06 | FK01-FK06 |
| MAP1-MAP3 | MK01-MK06, MK12, MK18, MK19 |
| V-03 עד V-11 | V+21, V+22, V+23 |
| VAP1-VAP3 | VD01-VD06 |
| XD01-XD07 | XK01-XK07 |

במקרה הטוב, הזנת קוד מהטבלה מנתבת ל-Transaction BP — הטרנזקציה הראשית לכל ה-business partner (כולל ספק ולקוח).
‏Transaction BP היא נקודת הכניסה היחידה ליצירה, עריכה, והצגה של business partners, ‏customers, ו-vendors. מספר ה-business partner מחליף את מספרי הספק והלקוח — השלכות על שדרוג/המרה. אך אין לקרוס את כל הטרנזקציות ב-ERP ל-BP (יש פונקציונליות ב-ERP שאינה ב-BP).
ב-S/4HANA, כל הטרנזקציות, דוחות, ו-condition records המשתמשים במספר customer/vendor כשדה קלט — דורשים את מספר ה-customer/vendor, לא ה-business partner. גם אם הוקצה business partner חדש, מספר ה-customer/vendor הקודם נדרש.

**הערת יועץ:** מודל ה-BP: ישות אחת, תפקידים מרובים (ספק+לקוח+עובד — דוגמת ה-foster care), קטגוריות (ארגון/אדם/קבוצה), ושיתוף נתונים כלליים בין roles. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, ⚠️ המוקש התפעולי: טרנזקציות ותיקות עדיין דורשות את מספר ה-customer/vendor הישן, לא את מספר ה-BP — שני עולמות-מספור חיים במקביל, וההדרכה חייבת לכסות זאת או שהתמיכה תוצף. יועץ מתעד את מיפוי-המספרים (BP↔vendor↔customer) ומנגיש אותו לכל המשתמשים.

sections.title: Loading Supplier Records in SAP S/4HANA
sections.en: 4.3.2 Loading Supplier Records in SAP S/4HANA For previous versions of SAP ERP, the standard data migration loading tool used most frequently was the Legacy System Migration Workbench (LSMW). Per SAP Note 2287723, LSMW is not the recommended option for SAP S/4HANA on-premise imple- mentations, however, and not even available as an option for SAP S/4HANA Cloud. The recommended options are listed in Table 4.4. For more information on migration and data loading approaches for on-premise SAP S/4HANA, visit https://rapid.sap.com/bp/RDM_S4H_OP. The next section reviews the data contained in a supplier master in the business partner. Source System On-Premise SAP S/4HANA SAP S/4HANA Cloud SAP R/3  SAP Data Services  SAP Information Steward  Rapid data migration con- tent (available for both SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud)  SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit and SAP S/4HANA migration object modeler  SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit  For SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition, the migration object modeler is also available SAP ERP Third-party ERP system Table 4.4 Data Migration Tool Options for SAP S/4HANA 4 Master Data 122
sections.he:
לגרסאות ERP קודמות, כלי ה-migration הנפוץ היה Legacy System Migration Workbench (LSMW). לפי SAP Note 2287723, ‏LSMW אינו מומלץ ל-on-premise S/4HANA, ואף לא זמין ל-S/4HANA Cloud. האפשרויות המומלצות ב-טבלה 4.4.
למידע על migration: ‏https://rapid.sap.com/bp/RDM_S4H_OP.

**טבלה 4.4 — אפשרויות כלי Data Migration ל-S/4HANA:**
| מקור | On-Premise S/4HANA | S/4HANA Cloud |
|---|---|---|
| SAP R/3 / SAP ERP / Third-party ERP | SAP Data Services; ‏SAP Information Steward; ‏Rapid data migration content; ‏SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit + migration object modeler | SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit; ל-private edition, גם migration object modeler |

טבלת-הכלים הזו מסמנת חילוף-דורות שחשוב להפנים: ה-LSMW — סוס-העבודה הוותיק של טעינות-הנתונים בעולם ה-ERP — אינו מומלץ עוד ל-on-premise S/4HANA ‏(SAP Note 2287723) וכלל אינו זמין בענן; במקומו, מפת-הכלים החדשה: ‏SAP Data Services ו-SAP Information Steward לחילוץ, ניקוי ואיכות-נתונים בקנה-מידה, תכני ה-rapid data migration המוכנים (זמינים לשני העולמות), וה-migration cockpit עם ה-migration object modeler — צמד-הליבה החדש: ה-cockpit מספק אובייקטי-טעינה מוכנים עם תבניות וולידציות, וה-modeler מאפשר להרחיבם בשדות מותאמים (זמין on-premise וב-private edition). ההשלכה הפרויקטלית: צוותים שמגיעים עם מיומנויות-LSMW ותיקות חייבים הסבה — וזה דווקא שדרוג: ה-cockpit כופה משמעת שה-LSMW רק המליץ עליה (ולידציות מובנות, מיפוי מתועד). והקישור שהטקסט נותן ‏(rapid.sap.com/bp/RDM_S4H_OP) הוא נקודת-הפתיחה לתכני-ההגירה המוכנים. הכלל המעשי: את כלי-הטעינה בוחרים לפי היעד (ענן = cockpit בלבד) ולפי מורכבות-הניקוי (נתונים מלוכלכים = ‏Data Services לפני הכול) — לא לפי הרגל.

**הערת יועץ:** חילוף-דורות בטעינות: ‏LSMW לא מומלץ (SAP Note 2287723) ולא קיים בענן; במקומו — ‏migration cockpit + object modeler, ‏Data Services ו-Information Steward לניקוי, ותכני rapid data migration. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, בוחרים כלי לפי יעד (ענן = cockpit) ולפי לכלוך-הנתונים (מלוכלך = ‏Data Services קודם) — לא לפי הרגל-LSMW. יועץ מתכנן את הסבת-מיומנויות-הצוות כחלק מהפרויקט, ומנצל את הוולידציות המובנות של ה-cockpit כשער-איכות.

sections.title: Setting Up the Supplier Master
sections.en: 4.3.3 Setting Up the Supplier Master Also known as the vendor master in SAP ERP, the supplier master contains the core data about the supplier used to conduct transactions. The supplier master contains the fol- lowing information:  General data, such as name, address, and bank information, as shown in Figure 4.15.  Purchasing data, such as the type of products supplied, the assigned purchasing organization, tax ID, incoterms/terms of payment, and several other related fields.  Accounting data, such as reconciliation account, creditor number, and payment methods. The reconciliation account number is for a general ledger account depict- ing the liabilities with regards to several vendors. The creditor number is assigned either automatically by the system or manually upon creation of the vendor master and is used as the subsidiary ledger number in financial accounting. In subledger accounting, total liabilities are calculated by vendor, rather than the process in gen- eral ledger accounting in which the liabilities are calculated for a group of vendors in that specific general ledger account. The reconciliation account is derived from the vendor master record upon entry of an invoice during the payment process. Figure 4.15 Bank Information Tab in SAP S/4HANA: Transaction BP © 123 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model The supplier master record in SAP S/4HANA includes a customer master component now that the supplier master and customer master are unified in Transaction BP. There is some baseline configuration required to set up the supplier master in the system. The updated business partner configuration guides and steps are available at ser- vice.sap.com. These steps should be completed prior to loading and/or entering sup- plier masters into the SAP S/4HANA environment. These configuration steps for customer/vendor setup are general guidelines for an on-premise implementation; you should always check online for the latest updates to any configuration steps and view recommendations for the version of SAP S/4HANA you’re implementing. Your project should determine customer-specific entries and steps in conjunction with sales and distribution stakeholders and owners in that project stream. Substantial configuration is required for business partner setup in SAP S/4HANA, as well as the follow-on conversion scenarios for CVI. The next section outlines the busi- ness partner conversion steps in more detail, as well as the business partner setup required in each phase of the project.
sections.he:
הידוע גם כ-vendor master ב-ERP, ה-supplier master מכיל את נתוני הליבה. כולל:
• **General data** — שם, כתובת, ומידע בנק (Figure 4.15).
• **Purchasing data** — סוג המוצרים, ה-purchasing organization, ‏tax ID, ‏incoterms/terms of payment, ועוד.
• **Accounting data** — ‏reconciliation account, ‏creditor number, ושיטות תשלום. ה-reconciliation account הוא GL account המתאר את ההתחייבויות מול ספקים רבים. ה-creditor number מוקצה אוטומטית/ידנית ומשמש כ-subsidiary ledger ב-FI. ב-subledger accounting, ההתחייבויות מחושבות לפי ספק (בניגוד ל-GL בו מחושבות לקבוצת ספקים). ה-reconciliation account נגזר מרשומת הספק בהזנת invoice.
ה-supplier master ב-S/4HANA כולל רכיב customer master (מאוחדים ב-Transaction BP). נדרשת תצורת baseline. מדריכי התצורה העדכניים ב-service.sap.com — לפני טעינה/הזנה. אלו הנחיות כלליות ל-on-premise; בדקו תמיד עדכונים לגרסה. הפרויקט יקבע ערכים ספציפיים עם בעלי sales and distribution.
נדרשת תצורה משמעותית, וגם תרחישי ההמרה ל-CVI. הסעיף הבא — צעדי ההמרה.

שלוש שכבות-הנתונים של רשומת-הספק משרטטות את חלוקת-הבעלות הארגונית עליה: הנתונים הכלליים (שם, כתובת, בנקים) משותפים לכל התפקידים; נתוני-הרכש (סוגי-מוצרים, ‏purchasing organization, מזהה-מס, ‏incoterms ותנאי-תשלום) הם ממלכת הקניינים; ונתוני-החשבונאות — ובראשם ה-reconciliation account וה-creditor number — הם ממלכת הכספים, וכאן ההסבר שהטקסט נותן שווה הפנמה: ה-reconciliation account הוא חשבון-GL שמרכז את ההתחייבויות מול קבוצת-ספקים, בעוד שב-subledger ההתחייבויות מחושבות פר-ספק — והחשבון נגזר אוטומטית מרשומת-הספק בעת הזנת-חשבונית, כלומר טעות בהקצאתו מזרימה התחייבויות לחשבון הלא-נכון בדוחות. החידוש המבני: ב-S/4HANA רשומת-הספק כוללת גם רכיב customer master — הכול מאוחד בטרנזקציה ‏(BP) — ולכן ההקמה דורשת תצורת-baseline משמעותית ותיאום עם בעלי sales and distribution: אותה ישות עשויה להיות ספק ולקוח גם יחד, וההגדרות חייבות לחיות בשלום. וההמלצה המעשית של הטקסט — לבדוק את מדריכי-התצורה העדכניים לפני כל טעינה — אינה נימוס: מודל ה-BP ממשיך להתפתח בין גרסאות, ומדריך-אתמול עלול להחסיר שדה-חובה של היום.

**הערת יועץ:** שלוש שכבות ברשומת-הספק: כללי (שם, בנקים), רכש (POrg, מס, ‏incoterms, תנאי-תשלום), חשבונאות (reconciliation account — נגזר אוטומטית בהזנת-חשבונית! — ו-creditor number); הכול מאוחד ב-(BP) כולל רכיב-לקוח. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, טעות ב-reconciliation account = התחייבויות בחשבון שגוי בדוחות — קביעת-החשבונות היא סעיף-בדיקה חובה. יועץ מתאם את ההקמה עם sales and distribution (ישות = ספק וגם לקוח) ובודק מדריכי-תצורה עדכניים לפני כל טעינה.

sections.title: Performing Customer/Vendor Integration
sections.en: 4.3.4 Performing Customer/Vendor Integration The supplier master is arguably the most vital master data for procurement. Suppliers are the core of a purchasing document; without a source of supply defined, no purchasing document can be generated. This area has also changed significantly in SAP S/4HANA. This section will both cover the initial configuration and then provide a brief tutorial on creating suppliers. This section also covers the conversion steps for SAP S/4HANA busi- ness partners. Both vendor and customer steps are included in this section. Foundational Data Little has changed from previous versions of SAP ERP in how you set up the organiza- tion structure in SAP S/4HANA. However, in master data there is a significant change in how vendors are set up in SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management versus previous ver- sions of SAP ERP. The first change is that vendors are now definitively referred to as suppliers in SAP S/4HANA, but not in the naming convention for CVI. In SAP S/4HANA, customers and vendors are now centralized into a single business partner concept. The conversion process and nuances of CVI are further explained in the next sections. In previous versions of SAP ERP, a supplier and a customer could be the same company, but they could not share the same master data element. You had to create a supplier record and a customer record. Here, the system constraints were not reflecting the real- ity for many companies and government entities. A citizen today may provide the local government with services such as foster care services, submit invoices to the govern- ment, and also be a “customer” in the sense that they pay their street cleaning fees or water delivery services directly to the local government. Many companies today inter- act both as suppliers and customers with their business partners. A large manufacturer 4 Master Data 124 and an MRO distributor, for example, may buy from and sell to each other in large vol- umes as the manufacturer leverages the MRO distributor for plant maintenance prod- uct orders and sells to the distributor many of the items the manufacturer produces. In previous versions of SAP, both a customer and a supplier record needed to be created to represent these relationships. In SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management, only one business partner record is needed. Keeping all of these data elements in sync for both the customer and the supplier falls on CVI. CVI ensures that customer and vendor master data tables, such as core tables KN and LF, are updated automatically after a business partner is created/changed. Tables KN and LF are still populated in SAP S/4HANA as they are in SAP ERP. Some other caveats of CVI and business partner design in SAP S/4HANA are as follows:  The customer/vendor hierarchy remains the same as in SAP ERP.  To create a customer or supplier record in SAP S/4HANA via an interface, the inter- face must call customer/vendor creation BAPI CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN.  Business partner data for retail systems such as SAP Fashion Management and cus- tomer as consumer, as used in retail industry solution versions, are not part of the conversion at this point.  CVI is not mandatory for on-premise SAP S/4HANA Finance.  Mass maintenance is possible for customers and vendors via Transaction BP. Trans- actions XD99, XK99, and MASS are available in Transaction BP. For SAP S/4HANA 1511, implementation of SAP Note 2346269 is required.  DEBMAS, an IDoc used for updating customer information, and CREMAS, an IDoc used for updating supplier information, can be used in SAP S/4HANA on premise 1610 and in 1511 if you implement SAP Note 2312529.  To get nine additional customer/vendor data structures, you need to implement SAP Notes 2324208 and 2331298, then run reports NOTE_2324208_DDIC and NOTE_ 2331298 to activate the DDIC structure changes. Program LSMW will need to be mod- ified to include the input data structure.  Custom code calls to old transactions are automatically redirected to the new ver- sions. You don’t need to change the custom code for this area. However, interfaces creating customer or vendor master data have to call the CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN or BusinessPartnerSUITEBulkReplicateRequest or BusinessPartnerRelationshipSUITEBulk- ReplicateRequest webservice rather than a previous function module and/or webser- vice. If you have interfaces that rely on previous function modules from SAP ERP, the code will need to be changed to call CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN or the aforementioned webservice, and mapping logic to new and/or custom fields may be required. To acti- vate CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN, implement SAP Note 2405714 for RFC_CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN enhancements. You can also navigate to Transaction BP in SAP S/4HANA by calling BUP_PARTNER_MAINTAIN from an external application. © 125 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model  If you’re running SAP S/4HANA alongside SAP ERP environments in your landscape, core interfaces (CIFs) to and from SAP S/4HANA for business partners are still sup- ported, as are middleware programs for business partner synchronization and SAP BW reporting on customers and vendors.  For converting credit management data, go to IMG path Migration to SAP S/4HANA Finance  Data Migration  Credit Management Migration.  For converting employees to business partners, see SAP Note 2340095. The implementation process with regards to vendors and CVI is outlined in Figure 4.16. During a greenfield implementation, in which no legacy ERP system is being converted directly to SAP S/4HANA, a data conversion nonetheless would take place if you were loading supplier or customer records into SAP S/4HANA. You need to upload these sup- plier records via CVI if this is the case. For conversion of an existing environment run- ning SAP Business Suite on SAP HANA, you need to convert the suppliers and customer records in the system to business partners first, then initiate the overall conversion to SAP S/4HANA. Figure 4.16 Process Flow for CVI Conversion Here you verify the configuration detailed at support.sap.com under Best Practice Building Block J61 for CVI Conversion (see https://support.sap.com/content/dam/SAAP/ Sol_Pack/Library/Configuration/J61_S4HANAX_BB_ConfigGuide_EN_XX.docx), or the corresponding version of these steps for your on-premise version of SAP S/4HANA. For SAP S/4HANA Cloud, the implementation team does not perform these steps. Before we jump into the tutorial, we should note that the customer record is required when initiating returns to a supplier in SAP S/4HANA. Therefore, you can’t ignore the customer records in the SAP ERP environment during a conversion process to SAP S/4HANA and CVI, and some cross-business collaboration with other stakeholders on Handover from Select Preparation Conversion Post-processing/Test Business Partner Business Partner Create change Customers Vendors Contacts Synchronization CVI Conversion CVI Synchronization SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA SAP S/4HANA Customers Vendors Contacts (KN*, LF*) Customers Vendors Contacts (KN*, LF*) SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Conversion Greenfield SAP S/4HANA Implementation Scenarios Business Partner upload Migration cockpit Data services Web service LSMW IDocs Manual CVI Configuration CVI Synchronization Business Partner 4 Master Data 126 the project and in the system outside of procurement (sales and distribution typically owns the customer master) must take place to ensure that full master data to support certain areas, including those required for returns, is in the new SAP S/4HANA environ- ment on go-live. To initiate the conversion process with CVI from SAP ERP to on-premise SAP S/4HANA, there are a couple of key items to keep in mind. First, we recommend archiving the business partners (customers and vendors) marked with the Deletion flag. Number ranges and numbering should also remain the same in the new system, if possible, to avoid confusion and mapping exercises (note that number ranges are a nontransport- able configuration item, as in previous releases of SAP ERP; you’ll need to perform manual configuration in each client, including production, to set the number ranges). SAP ERP must be at version 6.0 with enhancement pack levels of 0 to 7 to begin a con- version. If you have SAP ERP 6.0 EHP 0 to 4, you’ll need to apply SAP Note 2383051 if you have vendor contacts that need to be converted. For lower releases, EHP 1 to 3, you may either want to upgrade the EHP prior to conversion or create an incident message to obtain more guidance on conversion of vendor contacts. The CVI conversion steps from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA will be described in further detail ahead, beginning with the preparation phase. CVI Preparation Phase: SAP S/4HANA Vendor/Customer Conversion to Business Partners The first phase of a CVI conversion is preparation, as shown in Figure 4.17. The following tasks must be completed, many in conjunction with your technical team. As with the baseline configuration, we recommend that you check the latest conversion steps at support.sap.com based on the version of SAP S/4HANA to be implemented prior to pro- ceeding with a CVI conversion. Figure 4.17 CVI Conversion for On-Premise SAP S/4HANA and Greenfield Implementations Preparation Conversion Post Processing/Test • Pre-Check • SUM Activate Business Partner → Customer/Vendor • Activate BF • Check Customizing • CVI enhancements • CVI Configuration Test Synchronization Synchronization Cockpit Completion Check Consultants are involved in the transformation activities Application contacts are involved in the transformation activities SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA Greenfield implementation - Only post-processing/test step is required; follow Best Practice Building Block J6. © 127 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model In general, here are the steps you will follow: 1. Check and integrate customer/vendor enhancements. If you have any enhance- ments in the SAP ERP system being converted or planned in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem that would normally call an individual customer or vendor function module and/or transaction, these enhancement objects will need to be rewritten for the new business partner concept and functionality. 2. Activate business function CA_BP_SOA. This is typically done by your technical team via Cross Application Components  Enterprise Services and Business Functions  Acti- vate Business Functions, as shown in Figure 4.18. Figure 4.18 Activate CA_BP_SOA in Switch Framework 3. Perform CVI customizing, check customizing, and trigger necessary changes per the guides at support.sap.com. You can also dive deeper into business partner function- ality via a dedicated book from Rheinwerk Publishing titled Business Partners in SAP S/4HANA (see https://www.sap-press.com/business-partners-in-sap-s4hana_5468/). 4. Define number assignments according to the SAP S/4HANA conversion guide pro- vided at support.sap.com. 5. Maintain business partner mapping customizing and run the check report. In this step, you’ll map all of the business partner elements to their CVI counterparts. Fol- low menu path Cross-Application Components  Master Data Synchronization  Cus- tomer/Vendor Integration  Business Partner Settings  Settings for Customer Integration Field Assignment for Customer Integration  Assign Keys  Define Num- ber Assignment for Direction BP to Customer. After the number assignment map- ping from a business partner to a customer, shown in Figure 4.19, you then proceed with mapping a customer to a business partner. 4 Master Data 128 Figure 4.19 BP Number Assignment Direction to Customer 6. Finally, you map the attributes for a contact person, as shown in Figure 4.20, so that data such as legal form and legal status carry over seamlessly by following Cross- Application Components  Master Data Synchronization  Customer/Vendor Integra- tion  Business Partner Settings  Settings for Customer Integration  Field Assign- ment for Customer Integration  Assign Attributes. Figure 4.20 Assign Marital Statuses: Attributes Attribute Value Mapping Attribute value mapping must be maintained and must be equal for every existing cus- tomer instance. The IMG menu path is Cross-Application Components  Master Data Synchronization  Customer/Vendor Integration  Business Partner Settings  Settings for Customer Integration  Field Assignment for Customer Integration  Assign Attri- butes  Contact Person, followed by one of the options from the following lists. For the contact person:  Activate Assignment of Contact Persons  Assign Department Numbers for Contact Person © 129 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model  Assign Functions of Contact Person  Assign Authority of Contact Person  Assign VIP Indicator for Contact Person For the customer attributes:  Assign Marital Statuses  Assign Legal Form to Legal Status  Assign Payment Cards  Assign Industries For the Assign Industries option, the industry value mapping must be maintained and should be equal for every existing vendor instance; the industry assignment for the vendor and customer shares the same configuration table. Outbound industry map- ping maps the business partner to the customer/vendor, and inbound mapping maps the customer/vendor to the business partner. Now check and clean up customer/vendor data. Prior to initiating the conversion, this is an excellent time to tidy your supplier master records and customer records to pro- vide the new system with clean data. Follow these steps: 1. Archive vendors marked with the Deletion flag (optional; you can also convert these into the new system if preferred). 2. Download the following check reports: – 2216176: Pre- and postconversion check report Report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT – 1623677: CVI customizing check report Report CVI_FS_CHECK_CUSTOMIZING – 974504: Inconsistencies in link tables of master data sync check report – 2399368: Excel upload option in MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT (allow for customer/ven- dor selection upload from Excel for business partner conversion) 3. Check and integrate customer/vendor enhancements (see SAP Notes 2309153 and 1623809). The SAP Notes explain how to make customer enhancements to CVI (inte- grating additional customer/vendor fields in the business partner and using CVI synchronization to update them in the customer/vendor). 4. Activate business function CA_SUPPLIER_SOA, again using Transaction SFW5. 5. Switch to active status in CA_BP_SOA using the VENDOR_SFWS_SC1 and VENDOR_ SFWS_SC2 options in Cross Application Components  Enterprise Services and Busi- ness Functions  Activate Business Functions or Transaction SFW5, as in Figure 4.21, to allow the vendor contact person data to be synchronized with the business partner contact person data, and ensure that they have Global Status set to On. Also, you will need to verify SAP Note 1454441. 4 Master Data 130 Figure 4.21 Vendor Sync Switches Preparation Phase Customizing Tasks Next, perform the following customizing tasks: 1. Activate the postprocessing order request for the business partner synchronization object in IMG menu path Cross-Application Components  Master Data Synchroniza- tion  Synchronization Control  Synchronization Control  Activate PPO Requests for Platform Objects in the Dialog. 2. Activate the sync of the vendor, customer, and business partner under IMG menu path Cross-Application Components  Master Data Synchronization  Synchroniza- tion Control  Synchronization Control  Activate Synchronization Options, as shown in Figure 4.22. Figure 4.22 Activate Synchronization Options 3. Activate creation of postprocessing orders for accounts payable in IMG menu path SAP Banking  Colateral Management  General Settings  Postprocessing Office  Activate Creation of Postprocessing Orders, as shown in Figure 4.23. © 131 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model Figure 4.23 Activate Creation of Postprocessing Orders 4. Verify that the customer and vendor number ranges from the system to be con- verted do not overlap. If the number range settings do not overlap, they should be mirrored in the receiving system. If the number ranges do overlap, the number ranges in the receiving SAP S/4HANA system should be set so that most vendor and customer numbers can be reused. 5. If the numbers for customers and vendors should be taken into SAP S/4HANA busi- ness partner records, the number ranges in SAP S/4HANA for business partner, ven- dor, and customer must be set to External during the conversion and then set back to Internal upon completion of the conversion. The three IMG menu paths for locating the applicable number ranges are as follows: 1. Define number ranges for customers at IMG menu path Logistics—General  Busi- ness Partner  Customers  Control  Define and Assign Customer Number Ranges (see Figure 4.24). Figure 4.24 Define Customer Number Range Intervals Once you’ve defined the interval, you then assign this number range to the cus- tomer records as shown in Figure 4.25. 4 Master Data 132 Figure 4.25 Assign Customer Account Groups to Number Range 2. Follow the same steps for vendors by defining and then assigning number ranges via vendor IMG menu path Logistics—General  Business Partner  Vendor  Control  Define Number Ranges for Vendor Master Records. 3. Define number range groupings via IMG menu path Cross-Application Components  SAP Business Partner  Business Partner  Basic Settings  Number Ranges and Group- ings  Define Number Ranges/Define Groupings and Assign Number Ranges (see Fig- ure 4.26). Figure 4.26 Business Partner Groupings Overview Settings for Customer/Vendor Conversion to Business Partner Finally, you define the contact person business partner number range. This step is very important if you wish to maintain/convert contact persons successfully. CVI conver- sion report MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT assigns an internal business partner number to each contact person during conversion. The internal number range is the number range assigned to the internal standard grouping. If the assigned internal number range con- flicts with the targeted customer or vendor number ranges, then the number range for © 133 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model the contact person will need to be changed to a new range that doesn’t overlap with the range targeted for business partner numbers. Failure to set these number ranges cor- rectly can result in GUID error R1124: Business Partner with GUID Number X Does Not Exist. Customizing CVI Behavior with BAdIs In the event that you need to customize the CVI behavior, there are several Business Add-ins (BAdIs) provided for data assignment. Access them via IMG menu path Cross- Application Components  Master Data Synchronization  Customer/Vendor Integration  Business Partner Settings  Business Add-Ins (BAdIs). For business partner/customer/ vendor table field extension, see SAP Note 2309153, as well as SAP Note 2295823. Mapping is the next step in the preparation phase. The following steps need to be com- pleted and validated prior to gating out of the preparation phase: 1. For a customer, enter business partner roles FLCU00 (company data) and FLCU01 (sales data) under IMG menu path Cross-Application Components  Master Data Syn- chronization  Customer/Vendor Integration  Business Partner Settings  Settings for Customer Integration  Define BP Role for Direction Customer to BP. For vendors, the IMG menu path is the same as path for customers, but add the following at the end:  Settings for Vendor Integration  Define BP Role for Direction Vendor to BP. 2. For every customer and vendor account, a business partner grouping must be avail- able. This is set using menu path Cross-Application Components  Master Data Syn- chronization  Customer/Vendor Integration  Business Partner Settings  Settings for Customer Integration  Field Assignment for Customer Integration  Assign Keys  Define Number Assignment for Direction Customer to BP for customers, and the same path plus  Settings for Vendor Integration  Field Assignment for Vendor Inte- gration  Assign Keys  Define Number Assignment for Direction Vendor to BP for ven- dors. Running Final Reports You are now ready to run the reports prior to completing the preparation phase steps for the conversion: 1. The first report can be accessed via Transaction CVI_FS_CHECK_CUST and is used to check the customizing (see SAP Note 1623677). As with the mapping step, this report checks the customizing in both directions: customer/vendor to business partner and business partner to customer/vendor. This is done in SAP S/4HANA in postpro- cessing or in a greenfield implementation. 2. Report FSBP_IND_SECTOR_MAPPING_CHECK is optional; it checks and creates industry mapping entries for industry assignment in the context of CVI while eval- uating existing or missing assignment entries. If the number of industry values is low, this report is not required. 4 Master Data 134 3. Report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT, provided in SAP Note 2216176, is a pre- check report to check if all the mappings have been completed correctly. This report can be accessed via Transaction CVI_PRECHECK_UPGRADE. 4. Note that the CVI Mapping and Contact Person Mapping checkboxes are checked by default in report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT. They are used after business partner conversion to check if all customers/vendors/contact persons are con- verted. The report also checks whether business partner roles are assigned to account groups, whether the account groups are available, and the customer/vendor value mapping. The following SAP Notes can be used to automate the configuration steps and suppress the mandatory business partner field groups check during CVI conversion. All three SAP Notes have to be applied, even if you only need part of the functions (e.g., you need to suppress the mandatory business partner field groups check during CVI conversion but don’t need to use the automation feature):  2336018—BP S4HANA: Suppress Mandatory BP Field Groups Checks via MDS_ LOAD_COCKPIT Transaction  2345087—BP_BAP: Missing Values in Required Entry Fields Cause Posting Termina- tion in Mass Processing  2344034—S/4HANA: Automation for Master Data Migration If you want mandatory fields to throw error messages during migration, disable the mandatory field suppression feature. To do so, deactivate the CVI_MIGRATION_SUPPRESS_ CHK implementation of BAdI definition CVI_CUSTOM_MAPPER. Once all of the red light error messages have been resolved from the report and the yel- low error messages are reviewed, you can proceed to the CVI synchronization phase of the conversion to SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management. Synchronization Once you’ve completed and/or verified the preparation steps, you’re ready for the syn- chronization phase, as illustrated in Figure 4.27. Figure 4.27 Synchronization Phase Preparation Conversion Post Processing/Test • Pre-Check • SUM Activate Business Partner → Customer/Vendor Check CVI/Business Partner Customizing • Implement pre-checks • Activate BF Test Synchronization Synchronization Cockpit SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA © 135 4.3 SAP S/4HANA Business Partner Model During this phase, you will perform the following tasks: 1. Synchronize the data load according to the SAP S/4HANA Conversion Guide. 2. Review and resolve any errors due to data/customizing found in the Monitor tab. 3. Run postprocessing orders in the synchronization cockpit and verify the results with report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT. To begin, run report MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT, which creates a corresponding SAP busi- ness partner for the customer, vendor, and contact data for general data, addresses, role data, and bank details. In this report, you have the option to choose a customer and/or vendor conversion to a business partner or to filter by criteria such as account group and customer/vendor numbers. To expedite error analysis, we recommend running this report as a small batch initially in blocks of 10 to 50 customers/vendors. To resolve errors, click the postprocessing object (PPO) icon. This displays a master data error list. You can resolve these errors within the postprocessing object screen or out- side it, but the errors must be corrected to complete the conversion of the customer/ vendor and contact person. For more information on this and the synchronization cock- pit, be sure to check http://s-prs.co/500323 for the latest information and guidance. Once you’ve resolved the errors, you’re ready to review the conversion using the CVI_ PRECHECK_UPGRADE report and the PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT via report Transaction SE38. Execute these reports using the default selections, with the CVI Map- ping and Contact Person Mapping boxes checked as shown in Figure 4.28. Figure 4.28 Preupgrade Checks: Default Settings The CVI mapping checks whether all customers and vendors were mapped to a busi- ness partner, and the contact person mapping checks whether the contact persons have been converted to business partners. If you find inconsistencies, check SAP Note 974504. Once you’ve resolved any errors, run report MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT to complete the synchronization, then move on to the conversion phase. 4 Master Data 136 Conversion Phase The conversion phase (see Figure 4.29) is executed by the project’s technical team as part of the overall conversion from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA. No CVI activities are required during this phase. Figure 4.29 CVI Conversion Phase Postprocessing/Test Phase Once the technical team has completed the overall upgrade, the processing/test phase is all that remains (see Figure 4.30). In this phase, you verify the configuration detailed in Best Practice Building Block for CVI Conversion, which can be found at sup- port.sap.com under Central Configuration of Business Partners (J61) (see https://s- prs.co/500324). Ensure that these configuration settings have been made prior to test- ing. If your project is not based on best practice building blocks, then this guide should be used as a general reference only. Actual configuration may be determined based on your project design considerations. Figure 4.30 CVI Conversion: Postprocessing/Test Once your testing is complete, you’ve completed the CVI conversion, which is one of the major steps in moving from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, both from a design standpoint and in terms of conversion effort. Other master data setup/conversion, such as for material masters, isn’t nearly as involved. Preparation Conversion Post Processing/Test • Pre-Check • SUM Activate Business Partner → Customer/Vendor Check CVI/Business Partner Customizing • Implement pre-checks • Activate BF Test Synchronization Synchronization Cockpit SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA Preparation Conversion Post Processing/Test • Pre-Check • SUM Activate Business Partner → Customer/Vendor Check CVI/BP Customizing • Implement pre-checks • Activate BF Test Synchronization Synchronization Cockpit SAP ERP SAP S/4HANA © 137
sections.he:
ה-supplier master הוא נתון האב החיוני ביותר לרכש. ספקים הם ליבת מסמך הרכש; ללא מקור אספקה, אין מסמך. תחום זה השתנה משמעותית ב-S/4HANA. הסעיף מכסה תצורה ראשונית, יצירת ספקים, וצעדי ההמרה ל-business partners (ספקים ולקוחות).

**Foundational Data:**
מעט השתנה בהקמת המבנה הארגוני, אך באב יש שינוי משמעותי. ‏vendors נקראים כעת suppliers ב-S/4HANA (לא ב-CVI). לקוחות ו-vendors ממורכזים ל-business partner יחיד.
ב-ERP, ספק ולקוח יכלו להיות אותה חברה אך לא לחלוק רשומת אב — נדרשו שתי רשומות. אזרח עשוי לספק שירותים (foster care), להגיש invoices, וגם להיות "לקוח" (אגרות). יצרן ומפיץ MRO קונים ומוכרים זה לזה. ב-SAP S/4HANA, נדרשת רשומת business partner אחת בלבד.
סנכרון כל האלמנטים מוטל על CVI. ‏CVI מבטיח שטבלאות ה-customer/vendor (טבלאות הליבה KN ו-LF) מתעדכנות אוטומטית. ‏KN ו-LF עדיין מאוכלסות ב-S/4HANA כמו ב-ERP. הסתייגויות:
• היררכיית ה-customer/vendor נשארת כמו ב-ERP.
• ליצירת customer/supplier דרך ממשק, הממשק חייב לקרוא ל-BAPI ‏CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN.
• נתוני business partner למערכות retail (SAP Fashion Management, ‏customer as consumer) אינם חלק מההמרה כעת.
• ‏CVI אינו חובה ל-on-premise S/4HANA Finance.
• ‏mass maintenance אפשרי דרך Transaction BP. ‏Transactions XD99, ‏XK99, ו-MASS זמינים ב-BP. ל-S/4HANA 1511, נדרש SAP Note 2346269.
• ‏DEBMAS (IDoc לעדכון לקוח) ו-CREMAS (IDoc לעדכון ספק) ניתנים לשימוש ב-on-premise 1610, וב-1511 עם SAP Note 2312529.
• לתשעה מבני נתונים נוספים, יישמו SAP Notes 2324208 ו-2331298, ואז הריצו דוחות NOTE_2324208_DDIC ו-NOTE_2331298. ‏LSMW יידרש שינוי.
• קריאות custom code לטרנזקציות ישנות מנותבות אוטומטית. אך ממשקים היוצרים customer/vendor חייבים לקרוא ל-CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN או webservice ‏BusinessPartnerSUITEBulkReplicateRequest / BusinessPartnerRelationshipSUITEBulkReplicateRequest. להפעלת CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN, יישמו SAP Note 2405714 (RFC_CVI_EI_INBOUND_MAIN). ניתן לנווט ל-BP דרך קריאת BUP_PARTNER_MAINTAIN.
• אם מריצים S/4HANA לצד ERP, ‏CIFs ל-business partners עדיין נתמכים, וכן middleware לסנכרון ו-SAP BW reporting.
• להמרת credit management: ‏IMG • Migration to SAP S/4HANA Finance • Data Migration • Credit Management Migration.
• להמרת עובדים ל-business partners: ‏SAP Note 2340095.
תהליך היישום מתואר ב-Figure 4.16. ב-greenfield (ללא המרת ERP), המרת נתונים עדיין מתרחשת בטעינת ספקים/לקוחות — דרך CVI. להמרת סביבה קיימת (Business Suite on HANA), יש להמיר תחילה את הספקים והלקוחות ל-business partners, ואז ההמרה הכוללת.
ראו Best Practice Building Block J61 ל-CVI Conversion. ל-S/4HANA Cloud, צוות היישום אינו מבצע צעדים אלו.
הערה: רשומת ה-customer נדרשת ליזימת החזרות לספק ב-S/4HANA. לכן אין להתעלם מרשומות הלקוח ב-ERP בהמרה (sales and distribution בעלי ה-customer master).
ליזימת ההמרה מ-ERP ל-on-premise S/4HANA: ‏(1) מומלץ לארכב business partners עם Deletion flag; ‏(2) ה-number ranges והמספור צריכים להישאר זהים (ה-number ranges הם פריט תצורה לא-בר-transport — תצורה ידנית בכל client, כולל production). ‏SAP ERP חייב 6.0 עם EHP 0–7. ל-EHP 0–4, יישמו SAP Note 2383051 אם יש vendor contacts. ל-EHP 1–3, שדרגו או פתחו incident.

**CVI Preparation Phase — המרת Vendor/Customer ל-Business Partners:**
השלב הראשון — preparation (Figure 4.17). הצעדים:
1. בדקו ושלבו customer/vendor enhancements. ‏enhancements הקוראים ל-function module/transaction של customer/vendor יידרשו כתיבה מחדש ל-business partner.
2. הפעילו business function CA_BP_SOA, דרך Cross Application Components • Enterprise Services and Business Functions • Activate Business Functions (Figure 4.18).
3. בצעו CVI customizing, בדקו, והפעילו שינויים (מדריכי support.sap.com). ספר ייעודי: ‏Business Partners in SAP S/4HANA.
4. הגדירו number assignments לפי מדריך ההמרה.
5. תחזקו business partner mapping והריצו check report. מפו את כל אלמנטי ה-business partner למקבילות CVI. ‏Cross-Application Components • Master Data Synchronization • Customer/Vendor Integration • Business Partner Settings • Settings for Customer Integration • Field Assignment for Customer Integration • Assign Keys • Define Number Assignment for Direction BP to Customer (Figure 4.19). ואז customer ל-BP.
6. מפו את ה-attributes לאיש קשר (Figure 4.20) — legal form/status — דרך ... • Field Assignment for Customer Integration • Assign Attributes.

**Attribute Value Mapping:**
חייב תחזוקה ושוויון לכל customer instance. ‏IMG • Cross-Application Components • Master Data Synchronization • Customer/Vendor Integration • Business Partner Settings • Settings for Customer Integration • Field Assignment for Customer Integration • Assign Attributes • Contact Person, ואז אחת מהאפשרויות:
לאיש הקשר: ‏Activate Assignment of Contact Persons; ‏Assign Department Numbers; ‏Assign Functions; ‏Assign Authority; ‏Assign VIP Indicator.
ל-customer attributes: ‏Assign Marital Statuses; ‏Assign Legal Form to Legal Status; ‏Assign Payment Cards; ‏Assign Industries.
ל-Assign Industries, ה-mapping חייב שוויון לכל vendor instance (ה-vendor וה-customer חולקים טבלת תצורה). ‏outbound ממפה BP ל-customer/vendor; ‏inbound ממפה customer/vendor ל-BP.
כעת נקו נתוני customer/vendor (זמן מצוין לסדר):
1. ארכבו vendors עם Deletion flag (אופציונלי).
2. הורידו check reports:
  – 2216176: ‏pre/post-conversion (report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT)
  – 1623677: ‏CVI customizing (report CVI_FS_CHECK_CUSTOMIZING)
  – 974504: אי-עקביות בטבלאות הקישור
  – 2399368: ‏Excel upload ב-MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT
3. בדקו ושלבו enhancements (SAP Notes 2309153, 1623809).
4. הפעילו business function CA_SUPPLIER_SOA (Transaction SFW5).
5. הפעילו ב-CA_BP_SOA את VENDOR_SFWS_SC1 ו-VENDOR_SFWS_SC2 (Cross Application Components • Enterprise Services and Business Functions • Activate Business Functions או Transaction SFW5; ‏Figure 4.21), עם Global Status = On. ודאו SAP Note 1454441.

**Preparation Phase Customizing Tasks:**
1. הפעילו postprocessing order request: ‏Cross-Application Components • Master Data Synchronization • Synchronization Control • Synchronization Control • Activate PPO Requests for Platform Objects in the Dialog.
2. הפעילו sync של vendor/customer/business partner: ‏... • Synchronization Control • Activate Synchronization Options (Figure 4.22).
3. הפעילו יצירת PPO ל-AP: ‏SAP Banking • Collateral Management • General Settings • Postprocessing Office • Activate Creation of Postprocessing Orders (Figure 4.23).
4. ודאו שה-number ranges של customer/vendor אינם חופפים. אם לא — שקפו בקבלה. אם חופפים — קבעו כך שרוב המספרים ניתנים לשימוש חוזר.
5. אם המספרים יילקחו ל-S/4HANA, קבעו את ה-number ranges (business partner, ‏vendor, ‏customer) ל-External בהמרה ואז חזרה ל-Internal.
שלושת נתיבי ה-IMG ל-number ranges:
1. customers: ‏Logistics—General • Business Partner • Customers • Control • Define and Assign Customer Number Ranges (Figure 4.24), ואז הקצאה (Figure 4.25).
2. vendors: ‏Logistics—General • Business Partner • Vendor • Control • Define Number Ranges for Vendor Master Records.
3. groupings: ‏Cross-Application Components • SAP Business Partner • Business Partner • Basic Settings • Number Ranges and Groupings • Define Number Ranges / Define Groupings and Assign Number Ranges (Figure 4.26).
לבסוף, הגדירו את ה-number range של איש הקשר. חשוב מאוד. דוח ההמרה MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT מקצה מספר BP פנימי לכל איש קשר. ה-internal number range הוא של ה-internal standard grouping. אם מתנגש — שנו אותו לטווח שאינו חופף. כשל יגרום לשגיאת GUID R1124: ‏Business Partner with GUID Number X Does Not Exist.

**Customizing CVI Behavior with BAdIs:**
להתאמת CVI, יש BAdIs ל-data assignment: ‏IMG • Cross-Application Components • Master Data Synchronization • Customer/Vendor Integration • Business Partner Settings • Business Add-Ins (BAdIs). להרחבת שדות business partner/customer/vendor, ‏SAP Notes 2309153 ו-2295823.
ה-mapping הוא הצעד הבא. הצעדים לפני סיום ה-preparation:
1. ל-customer, הזינו business partner roles ‏FLCU00 (company data) ו-FLCU01 (sales data): ‏Cross-Application Components • Master Data Synchronization • Customer/Vendor Integration • Business Partner Settings • Settings for Customer Integration • Define BP Role for Direction Customer to BP. ל-vendors, אותו נתיב + Settings for Vendor Integration • Define BP Role for Direction Vendor to BP.
2. לכל חשבון customer/vendor נדרש business partner grouping: ‏... • Settings for Customer Integration • Field Assignment for Customer Integration • Assign Keys • Define Number Assignment for Direction Customer to BP, וה-vendor equivalent.

**Running Final Reports:**
מוכנים להריץ דוחות לפני סיום ה-preparation:
1. ‏Transaction CVI_FS_CHECK_CUST — בדיקת ה-customizing (SAP Note 1623677). בודק בשני הכיוונים.
2. ‏Report FSBP_IND_SECTOR_MAPPING_CHECK (אופציונלי) — בודק ויוצר industry mapping. אם ערכי industry מעטים, לא נדרש.
3. ‏Report PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT (SAP Note 2216176) — בדיקה שכל ה-mappings הושלמו. דרך Transaction CVI_PRECHECK_UPGRADE.
4. ה-CVI Mapping ו-Contact Person Mapping מסומנים כברירת מחדל — בודקים לאחר ההמרה אם כל ה-customers/vendors/contact persons הומרו, אם roles מוקצים ל-account groups, וה-value mapping.
‏SAP Notes לאוטומציה ולדיכוי בדיקת ה-mandatory field groups (יש ליישם את כל השלושה):
• 2336018 — דיכוי mandatory BP field groups ב-MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT
• 2345087 — ערכים חסרים גורמים לביטול posting
• 2344034 — אוטומציה ל-master data migration
אם רוצים שדות חובה ייתנו שגיאות, השביתו את הדיכוי — בטלו את CVI_MIGRATION_SUPPRESS_CHK של BAdI ‏CVI_CUSTOM_MAPPER.
לאחר פתרון השגיאות האדומות וסקירת הצהובות, ניתן להמשיך ל-synchronization.

**Synchronization:**
לאחר ה-preparation, מוכנים ל-synchronization (Figure 4.27):
1. סנכרנו את ה-data load לפי המדריך.
2. סקרו ופתרו שגיאות בלשונית Monitor.
3. הריצו postprocessing orders ב-synchronization cockpit ואמתו עם PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT.
הריצו report MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT — יוצר business partner מתאים לנתוני customer/vendor/contact. ניתן לבחור המרת customer/vendor או לסנן (account group, מספרים). לזירוז ניתוח השגיאות, הריצו בבלוקים של 10–50.
לפתרון שגיאות, לחצו על אייקון ה-PPO (postprocessing object) — רשימת שגיאות. יש לתקנן.
לאחר התיקון, סקרו עם CVI_PRECHECK_UPGRADE ו-PRECHECK_UPGRADATION_REPORT (Transaction SE38), עם CVI Mapping ו-Contact Person Mapping מסומנים (Figure 4.28).
ה-CVI mapping בודק שכל ה-customers/vendors מופו ל-business partner; ‏contact person mapping בודק את ההמרה. לאי-עקביות, ‏SAP Note 974504. לאחר התיקון, הריצו MDS_LOAD_COCKPIT לסיום הסנכרון, ועברו ל-conversion.

**Conversion Phase:**
ה-conversion (Figure 4.29) מבוצע ע"י הצוות הטכני כחלק מההמרה הכוללת. אין פעולות CVI בשלב זה.

**Postprocessing/Test Phase:**
לאחר השדרוג הכולל, נותר ה-processing/test (Figure 4.30). אמתו את התצורה ב-Best Practice Building Block ל-CVI Conversion (Central Configuration of Business Partners [J61]). ודאו את ההגדרות לפני הבדיקה. אם הפרויקט אינו מבוסס best practice, השתמשו במדריך כהפניה כללית בלבד.
בסיום הבדיקה, השלמתם את ה-CVI conversion — אחד הצעדים העיקריים במעבר ל-S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement. הקמת/המרת אב אחרת (material masters) פחות מורכבת.

**הערת יועץ:** ה-CVI — הצעד המרכזי במעבר: ‏vendors→suppliers, איחוד לקוחות-וספקים ל-BP, תצורה יסודית, יצירה והמרה עם בדיקות. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, זהו תת-הפרויקט המסוכן של נתוני-האב: איכות רשומות-המקור (כפילויות, שדות-זבל, ספקים מתים) נחשפת כאן במלואה — ולכן ניקוי לפני המרה, לא אחריה. יועץ מריץ המרת-פיילוט על מדגם, מודד שגיאות, מתקן כללים — ורק אז ממיר הכול; והמרה בלי dry-run מלא = הימור על נתון-האב הקריטי ביותר.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 4.4 Summary 4.4 Summary Master data and transactional data designs underpin and simplify system usage in SAP S/4HANA environments when implemented in a thoughtful manner. Driving a level of granularity in the material masters that is not required for the business leads to user frustration when they try and find the appropriate material master to use in a transac- tion, as well the additional maintenance to enact any changes to the material masters. For material groups, not designing a structured system of classification up front can lead to reporting challenges down the line as users misclassify materials and purchas- ing departments lack clear views into what types of items are being consumed and used in production activities. These were all key areas in previous iterations of SAP ERP. One area that differs in SAP S/4HANA is the business partner record. SAP S/4HANA introduces a significant change to how supplier and customer masters are managed in the system. These two types of partner functions in SAP S/4HANA are unified into a business partner concept, which has ramifications for conversions and upgrades from previous versions of SAP ERP and for usage of the master record in purchasing transactions in SAP S/4HANA. With master data addressed, the next chapter shifts focus to operational procurement and the base-level types of transactions in purchasing. ©
sections.he:
עיצובי נתוני האב והנתונים הטרנזקציוניים מבססים ומפשטים את השימוש ב-S/4HANA כשמיושמים במחשבה. פירוט-יתר ב-material masters → תסכול ותחזוקה נוספת. ל-material groups, אי-עיצוב מערכת סיווג מובנית מראש → אתגרי דיווח (משתמשים מסווגים שגוי, מחלקות הרכש חסרות נראות).
אלו היו תחומי מפתח באיטרציות קודמות. תחום שונה ב-S/4HANA — ה-business partner record. ‏S/4HANA משנה משמעותית כיצד supplier ו-customer masters מנוהלים — מאוחדים למושג ה-business partner, עם השלכות על המרות ושדרוגים, ועל השימוש ברשומת האב בטרנזקציות.
הפרק הבא — operational procurement וסוגי הטרנזקציות הבסיסיים ברכש.

סיכום-הפרק קושר את שלושת החוטים לעיקרון אחד: נתוני-אב מעוצבים-במחשבה הם שמפשטים את המערכת — ושני כשלי-העיצוב שהוא חוזר ומזהיר מפניהם הם בדיוק הנפוצים בשטח: פירוט-יתר ב-material masters, שמתגלה כתסכול-משתמשים בחיפוש הרשומה הנכונה וכעומס-תחזוקה בכל שינוי; וסיווג-רופף ב-material groups, שמתגלה באיחור — כשמשתמשים מסווגים שגוי, הרכש מאבד נראות לצריכה, והדוחות הופכים לחסרי-משמעות. ההיגיון המשותף: שני הכשלים זולים למניעה בשלב-העיצוב ויקרים מאוד לתיקון אחרי שהצטברו טרנזקציות. והחוט השלישי — ה-business partner — הוא השינוי שמייחד את S/4HANA מהדורות הקודמים: איחוד רשומות הספק והלקוח למושג אחד, עם השלכות שנפרשו לאורך הפרק — על המרות ושדרוגים (ה-CVI כתת-פרויקט), על שילובי-ענן (Ariba שדורש את המודל), ועל העבודה היומיומית בטרנזקציות. עם התשתית הזו — חומרים מסווגים, אצוות וסריאלים היכן שנדרש, וספקים במודל האחוד — הספר עובר מהסטטיקה לדינמיקה: הפרק הבא פותח את ה-operational procurement וסוגי-הטרנזקציות הבסיסיים של הרכש.

**הערת יועץ וסיכום מורחב:** שלושת החוטים: עיצוב-במחשבה (פירוט-יתר בחומרים וסיווג-רופף בקבוצות = הכשלים הזולים-למניעה והיקרים-לתיקון), עקיבות מדורגת (batch/serial רק היכן שחובה), וה-business partner כשינוי-הדור (CVI, ‏Ariba, מספור כפול). ליועץ: פרק נתוני-האב הוא המקום שבו פרויקטים נשפטים בשנה השנייה — המערכת עולה עם כל תצורה, אבל חיה או מתה על איכות-האב. הכלל המסכם: כל שדה, קבוצה ורמת-עקיבות חייבים הצדקה עסקית — והממשל (מי-יוצר-מה) מתועד וחתום. הבא: ‏operational procurement — הטרנזקציות עצמן.

sections.title: What Is Operational Procurement?
sections.en: 5.1 What Is Operational Procurement? Operational procurement supports the day-to-day processes of an organization via tac- tical procurement of services and materials, often by a casual user purchasing for a department’s needs or even their own role-specific ones. For example, a casual user may need to order a new laptop or IT equipment in order to perform their job. An office 5 Operational Procurement 140 manager may need to order office supplies to keep an office stocked with paper, toner, and other supplies. These types of purchases can be driven by various parts of the orga- nization in high-frequency, low-value orders. From the onset, the mismatch of a complex solution designed to support complex pur- chasing for direct procurement and the casual, untrained user looking to conduct oper- ational procurement was sure to cause issues. There is nothing inherently wrong with having large amounts of detail in a Purchase Order or Requisitioning screen in a system used for heavy-duty industrial manufacturing. Often, this level of functionality is quite necessary—say, for Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) activities with a supplier or for complex items vital to the production process. But having complex, professional, buyer- and engineer-centric screens makes purchasing for the casual user a bit more cumbersome than optimal. Many of these screens can make it downright frustrating for an untrained user trying to order mundane supply items like pens and paper, as each field can issue a hard-to-understand warning message or hard-stop error, incor- rect entries quickly negate the entire document’s validity, and multiple tabs and steps have to be completed—all this for a simple order that costs perhaps $10. Using SAP S/4HANA for this kind of procurement often is akin to having to use an airplane cockpit and all of its controls to steer a bicycle. A casual user accustomed to sleek, online shop- ping experiences will quickly tire of trying to navigate a corporate procurement system designed to support direct procurement. One approach to operational procurement is to take the process out of ERP systems. Cloud solutions such as SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA and on-premise solutions such as SAP Supplier Relationship Management (SAP SRM) are examples of this approach. This allows a system to mask all of the complexity and the procurement options that aren’t applicable to a simple transaction, distilling for the user what is nec- essary to find items and create orders with the fewest clicks, entries, and headaches possible. This approach, especially in cloud-based applications, works very well for sim- plifying the UX and allowing even the most casual and untrained user to find what he’s looking for and order it without calls to the helpdesk or frustration. However, early in the transaction, these operational procurement systems are already dependent upon ERP, even if their UIs appear independent. First, calls need to be made from the procurement system back to the “mothership” ERP system to find out if the user is purchasing via a correct financial object in the finance and controlling system. Finance has to support a number of functions in SAP S/4HANA, so it can’t be moved into a standalone procurement solution without bring- ing all the other dependent modules with it or leading to an expensive, “interface spa- ghetti” scenario. The users themselves need to be managed in real time; terminated employees can’t be allowed to continue to make purchases on behalf of a company or government entity. For this, the purchasing system requires real-time updates from the HR system or a user-management system that deactivates users throughout the landscape immediately when they leave the company or government entity. © 141 5.1 What Is Operational Procurement? There also is the question of efficiency and avoiding unnecessary stock to consider. What if the user is looking for an item already held and available in a company or gov- ernment entity warehouse? If the operational procurement system and/or buyer can- not check this prior to assigning a source of supply and issuing a PO, excess stock may be purchased instead of consuming existing stock. Excess stock causes waste, ineffi- ciency, and, most alarmingly for a business, expense. If checking for existing stock needs to be a manual process step in a procurement system, buyers are focusing on per- forming manual tasks that could be automated in an integrated system, rather than strategic procurement activities that generate exponentially more savings and value for the firm or government entity. These issues pose a conundrum for operational procure- ment in SAP S/4HANA: running operational procurement directly in SAP S/4HANA can be quite difficult for casual users and from an IT landscape perspective, but it’s also the ideal place for procurement in many cases because all of the dependent modules and integration topics are already covered. The main stumbling block to operational procurement has always been usability and UI issues, as well as transactional volumes. An ERP system supporting operational pro- curement needs to be intuitive to use, minimize transaction steps while remaining flexible and capable of handling a diverse set of transactions, support catalog content, and support heavy volumes of low-dollar transactions, all while making the most of an ERP system’s native integrations with associated modules. Incidentally, these are the driving forces behind SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement’s embrace of opera- tional procurement as a core ERP process. SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement supports the operational purchaser across self-service requisitioning, requirement processing, PO processing, service purchasing and entry, and PO collaboration. Requisitions can be created directly by a user via a self-service procurement process or from a system/business process occurring in a module in SAP S/4HANA, such as an MRP run in which defined reorder points trigger the creation of a requisition—a bill of materials (BOM)—that requires an additional item to be ordered as part of the materi- als list or a project systems requirement generated from what’s called a network in proj- ect systems. A network in project systems tells the user what tasks need to be performed in sequence by a certain time. Automated procurement processes typically used in the procurement of items needed in production, known as direct procurement, will be discussed in Chapter 6. The focus in self-service requisitioning is on user-driven requisitioning, which is more typically found in indirect procurement. As illustrated in Figure 5.1, self-service procurement is part of the requisition-to-pay process flow. The requisition is the first document in the procurement chain that even- tually leads to a purchase order and/or contract, as well as follow-on documents, such as order confirmations, advance shipping notifications (ASNs), goods/service receipts (GRs), and invoices. 5 Operational Procurement 142 Figure 5.1 Operational Procurement: Requisition-to-Pay Process Flow There are three main types of procurement conducted in operational procurement: stock, consumables, and external services. All of these types of procurement can be used in other procurement scenarios. Stock procurement is typically used for direct procurement activities, such as the ones discussed in the next chapter, but you can pur- chase and take into inventory items such as office supplies and equipment that qualify as operational indirect items as well. Consumable items are directly in the wheelhouse of operational procurement. A consumable item is typically an indirect item that is con- sumed and replenished on an ongoing basis, often by the consumers themselves. Pens, paper, coffee for the office kitchen, and other types of consumables may be ordered by the office manager or directly by an employee who notices that the office needs more of a consumable good. Consumables often do not require a goods receipt or a valuated goods receipt used primarily for inventory management processes and valuations, as these consumable purchases are petty at an individual level. In aggregate, however, consumable purchasing can be quite significant for an organization, and a level of management in the system may thus be desirable, if not a necessity. External services procurement is the procurement of services to be delivered by indi- viduals or groups who are not employees of the organization, but only involved to deliver that particular scope of work. These services can support the direct side of the equation, but they can also comprise cleaning or gardening services for the grounds of the office, for example, making these external services indirect. Although an office manager may set up the purchasing documentation for external services relating to the office, a project manager may need to directly set up the purchasing framework for consultants being hired to support a project. The defining feature for operational procurement and for stock, consumable, and exter- nal procurement is that these types of procurement do not necessarily require a trained, dedicated buyer to initiate the requisition. The demand and consequent requesting in the system may come from the employee directly. When it does, this type of procure- ment is squarely in the category of operational procurement, and it follows that the solu- tion provided in system to support this activity must support its untrained and barely Supplier Confirmation Advanced Shipping Notification Invoice Requisition Purchase Order Goods/Services Receipt Customer Only Approvals Sourcing Customer/Supplier Document Exchange Supplier Quote, Catalog, Contract Approvals © 143
sections.he:
‏operational procurement תומך בתהליכים היומיומיים — רכש טקטי של שירותים וחומרים, לעיתים ע"י משתמש מזדמן הקונה לצרכי מחלקה או תפקיד. למשל laptop/ציוד IT, או office manager המזמין ציוד משרדי. הזמנות בתדירות גבוהה ובערך נמוך.
מלכתחילה, אי-ההתאמה בין פתרון מורכב (לרכש ישיר) למשתמש מזדמן ולא-מאומן גרמה לבעיות. אין פסול בכמות פירוט במסך PO/Requisitioning במערכת לייצור תעשייתי כבד (למשל ל-EDI עם ספק או פריטים קריטיים). אך מסכים מורכבים ממוקדי-buyer/engineer הופכים רכש למשתמש מזדמן למסורבל — כל שדה עשוי להוציא אזהרה או hard-stop, הזנה שגויה מבטלת את המסמך, ולשוניות וצעדים רבים — להזמנה של $10. כמו לטוס מטוס כדי לנווט אופניים. משתמש מזדמן הרגיל לחוויית קנייה online יתעייף.
גישה אחת — להוציא את התהליך מ-ERP. פתרונות ענן (SAP Ariba Buying for SAP S/4HANA) ו-on-premise (SAP SRM) הם דוגמאות. ממסך את המורכבות ומזקק למשתמש את הדרוש למינימום קליקים. עובד היטב לפישוט ה-UX. אך כבר מוקדם בטרנזקציה, מערכות אלו תלויות ב-ERP, גם אם ה-UI נראה עצמאי.
ראשית, קריאות ל-ERP ("mothership") לבדוק אם המשתמש קונה דרך אובייקט פיננסי נכון. ‏finance תומך בפונקציות רבות — לא ניתן להעבירו לפתרון עצמאי ללא כל המודולים התלויים (או "interface spaghetti"). המשתמשים מנוהלים בזמן-אמת — עובד שפוטר לא יכול להמשיך לקנות. נדרשים עדכונים מ-HR/user-management.
שיקול נוסף — יעילות ומניעת מלאי מיותר. מה אם הפריט כבר זמין במחסן? אם מערכת הרכש לא בודקת לפני הקצאת מקור והנפקת PO, ייקנה מלאי עודף — בזבוז והוצאה. אם הבדיקה ידנית, ה-buyers מתמקדים במשימות שניתן לאוטמט במקום רכש אסטרטגי. ‏conundrum — הרצת operational procurement ישירות ב-S/4HANA קשה למשתמשים מזדמנים ול-IT, אך גם המקום האידיאלי (המודולים התלויים מכוסים).
מכשול עיקרי — שמישות ו-UI, ונפחי טרנזקציה. מערכת ERP צריכה להיות אינטואיטיבית, למזער צעדים תוך גמישות, לתמוך ב-catalog, ולתמוך בנפחים גבוהים של עסקאות בערך נמוך, תוך מינוף האינטגרציות הנטיביות. אלו הכוחות מאחורי אימוץ ה-operational procurement כתהליך ליבה. ‏S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement תומך ב-operational purchaser ב-self-service requisitioning, ‏requirement processing, ‏PO processing, ‏service purchasing/entry, ו-PO collaboration.
‏requisitions נוצרים ישירות ע"י משתמש (self-service) או ממערכת/תהליך במודול — למשל MRP run בו reorder points מפעילים יצירת requisition, ‏BOM הדורש פריט נוסף, או דרישת project systems מ-network. ‏network ב-project systems אומר אילו משימות לבצע ברצף. רכש אוטומטי (direct procurement) — פרק 6. ב-self-service requisitioning, הדגש על user-driven requisitioning (נפוץ ברכש עקיף).
כפי שמוצג ב-Figure 5.1, ‏self-service procurement הוא חלק מה-requisition-to-pay. ה-requisition הוא המסמך הראשון, המוביל ל-PO ו/או contract, ומסמכי המשך (order confirmations, ‏ASNs, ‏GRs, ‏invoices).
שלושה סוגי רכש ב-operational procurement: ‏stock, ‏consumables, ו-external services. כולם ניתנים לשימוש בתרחישים אחרים. ‏stock procurement נפוץ לרכש ישיר, אך ניתן לרכוש ולהכניס למלאי גם פריטים עקיפים. ‏consumable הוא בליבת ה-operational — פריט עקיף הנצרך ומתחדש (עטים, נייר, קפה). לעיתים אינו דורש GR או valuated GR. במצרף, ‏consumable purchasing משמעותי.
‏external services procurement — רכש שירותים מאנשים/קבוצות שאינם עובדים. תומך בצד הישיר, אך גם עקיף (ניקיון/גינון). ‏office manager עשוי להקים את התיעוד; ‏project manager את ה-framework ליועצים.
המאפיין המגדיר ל-operational procurement (ו-stock/consumable/external) — אינם דורשים בהכרח buyer ייעודי ליזימת ה-requisition. הביקוש עשוי לבוא ישירות מהעובד. אז זה operational procurement, והפתרון חייב לתמוך במשתמשים לא-מאומנים — מה שהופך self-service לאפשרי ואף מהנה. זו מטרת S/4HANA.

**הערת יועץ:** ‏operational procurement = הרכש הטקטי היומיומי: תדירות גבוהה, ערך נמוך, משתמש מזדמן — ואי-ההתאמה ההיסטורית בין מסכי-ייצור-כבד למשתמש כזה היא שהולידה את ה-self-service. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, זיהוי קו-הגבול אצל הלקוח (מה מזדמן ומה מקצועי) הוא צעד-האפיון הראשון — כי כל צד מקבל חוויה אחרת. יועץ ממפה את פרופילי-המשתמשים לפני שנוגע בתצורה: מי מזמין, באיזו תדירות, ומה הוא מסוגל ללמוד.

sections.title: Self-Service Procurement
sections.en: 5.2 Self-Service Procurement trained users in a way that makes self-service procurement possible and even enjoyable. This is the goal of SAP S/4HANA with self-service procurement. 5.2 Self-Service Procurement In SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, users can create a requisition and identify appropriate sources of supply via a consumer-grade UX—that is, a UX like that users would find in their personal online shopping experiences (see Figure 5.2). Self-service requisitioning is completely supported with a UI built on SAP Fiori, with tiles and step simplification to enable a completely different UX from that found in traditional ERP requisitioning. Figure 5.2 Self-Service Requisitioning in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement Requisitions are internal documents a corporation or government entity uses to lay claim to a service or material—essentially, a formalized request for a supply or service. Requisitions can be created with or without a source of supply and with or without a material master or service master number. Figure 5.3 Shop on Behalf Requisition Functionality There are a number of key innovations around simplification and speed for self-service procurement in SAP S/4HANA. Most importantly, one-click ordering is the predomi- nant concept in this area, as personified in the new UI. The content search and dynamic filtering is built on SAP S/4HANA, allowing for vast performance improvements and usability over traditional ERP-based requisitioning. You can access catalog content like a punchout catalog in the SAP Ariba Catalog area, a third-party punchout catalog, as Operational Purchasing Purchase Order Collaboration Purchase Order Processing Requirements Processing Self-Service Requisitioning Service Purchasing and Entry Augmented Decision Making (SAP BTP) 5 Operational Procurement 144 well as catalog content loaded directly into SAP S/4HANA. Loading and indexing cata- logs in SAP S/4HANA allows for cross-catalog search directly in system. Finally, there is a catalog solution package created by SAP Consulting called the lean catalog, extending the native catalog functionality further in SAP S/4HANA and building upon the inte- gration advantages of catalogs maintained in SAP S/4HANA directly. You also have shop on behalf flexibility, where a user can select from a group of users when creating a requisition and order something on behalf of a colleague, as shown in Figure 5.3. In the following sections, we’ll look at some of the functionality available for self- service procurement.
sections.he:
(המשך 5.1) — זו מטרת S/4HANA עם self-service procurement.
ב-S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement, משתמשים יוצרים requisition ומזהים מקורות אספקה דרך UX ברמת-צרכן (כמו קנייה online; ‏Figure 5.2). ‏self-service requisitioning נתמך ב-UI מבוסס-Fiori, עם tiles ופישוט צעדים.
‏requisitions הם מסמכים פנימיים שהארגון משתמש בהם לתבוע שירות/חומר — בקשה רשמית. ניתן ליצור עם/בלי מקור אספקה ועם/בלי material/service master.
חידושי מפתח לפישוט ומהירות. החשוב ביותר — ‏one-click ordering. החיפוש והסינון הדינמי בנויים על S/4HANA (שיפורי ביצועים). ניתן לגשת ל-catalog content — ‏punchout ב-SAP Ariba Catalog, ‏punchout צד-שלישי, או תוכן שנטען ישירות. טעינה ואינדקס מאפשרים cross-catalog search. יש גם פתרון lean catalog (של SAP Consulting), המרחיב את הפונקציונליות הנטיבית. יש גם גמישות shop on behalf — בחירה מקבוצת משתמשים והזמנה עבור עמית (Figure 5.3).

ה-requisition — המסמך הפנימי שבו הארגון 'תובע' שירות או חומר — הוא גיבור הסעיף, והפיכתו לחוויית-קנייה צרכנית היא כל הסיפור: ה-UI מבוסס-ה-Fiori עם האריחים ופישוט-הצעדים נועד להתחרות בחוויה שהמשתמש מכיר מהקניות הפרטיות שלו, כי זה הרף האמיתי — עובד שמתקשה במערכת פשוט יעקוף אותה. שלושת חידושי-המפתח ראויים לפירוק: ה-one-click ordering מקצר את המסלול מבחירה להזמנה לצעד אחד; החיפוש והסינון הדינמיים רוכבים על שיפורי-הביצועים של הפלטפורמה — חיפוש שמרגיש מיידי ולא 'דוח שרץ'; ותשתית-הקטלוגים גמישה בשלושה מסלולים — ‏punchout ל-SAP Ariba Catalog, ‏punchout לקטלוגים צד-שלישי, או תוכן שנטען ואינדוקס מקומית — כשהטעינה-והאינדוקס הם שמאפשרים cross-catalog search: חיפוש אחד על-פני כל הקטלוגים במקום מסע בין אתרי-ספקים. פתרון ה-lean catalog (מבית SAP Consulting) מרחיב את היכולת הנטיבית, ו-shop on behalf משלים את התמונה התפעולית: מזכירה שמזמינה עבור מנהל, רכזת שמזמינה לצוות — בחירת המשתמש-הנהנה מקבוצה מוגדרת. השורה התחתונה: דרישה יכולה להיפתח עם או בלי מקור-אספקה ועם או בלי רשומת-אב — הגמישות הזו היא שמכסה את כל תרחישי הרכש המזדמן.

**הערת יועץ:** הדרישה כחוויית-קנייה: ‏Fiori, ‏one-click, קטלוגים בשלושה מסלולים (punchout ל-Ariba, צד-שלישי, טעינה מקומית עם cross-catalog search), ‏lean catalog, ו-shop on behalf. מנקודת-מבט מעשית, איכות-הקטלוגים היא הקובע: ‏self-service עם קטלוגים דלים = דרישות-טקסט-חופשי שמציפות קניינים. יועץ משקיע בתוכן לפני ההשקה — הקטלוג המלא הוא 80% מהחוויה, והרף הוא הקנייה הפרטית של המשתמש.

sections.title: Creating a Requisition or Shopping Cart in SAP S/4HANA
sections.en: 5.2.1 Creating a Requisition or Shopping Cart in SAP S/4HANA In Figure 5.4, the screen is simplified down to the bare essentials for creating a requisi- tion. Either a user elects to use a catalog to find the item or, if the item isn’t found in a catalog, the user can describe it. Note that the SAP Ariba Catalog solution can be embed- ded in this view, creating a seamless catalog experience even when the user is punch- ing out to a catalog area. To create a requisition for an operational procurement item or service, a user logs into the My Purchase Requisitions—New app, which deprecates the Create Purchase Requi- sitions app as of SAP S/4HANA 2022, and types in the item in the search bar. If the desired item doesn’t appear in the search results, the user can search using a different term or create a descriptive item by selecting the Create Item option (see Figure 5.4). Figure 5.4 SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement: Create Requisition App You can also order hierarchical line items. These can be activated in SAP S/4HANA 2022 and later and allow for both material and service items to be set up in a hierarchical manner. You can also order catalog items. Going into the lean catalog, you can select from numerous items and categories as shown in Figure 5.5. Note that once the sup- plier is assigned, the system can check automatically for trade compliance based on the © 145 5.2 Self-Service Procurement item selected and supplier being used. Presumably, in a catalog item this has already been validated and the items featured in the catalog are compliant. Figure 5.5 Lean Catalog Shopping Once the user has selected or described an item, she is ready to order the items in the shopping cart (see Figure 5.6). Figure 5.6 Selecting Item in Create Purchase Requisition 5 Operational Procurement 146 You can now order this item by clicking the Order button.
